title: Notation and Conventions
about: The single source for the project's notation and conventions. scripts/build_notation.py generates Aim/Common/Notation.tex from this file, and scripts/check_conventions.py enforces the rules marked enforced. Standard mathematical notation is not listed. The deviations table holds only the places where the Lean is written differently from standard mathematics; add a row when a Lean file first needs one.

variables.note: the ambient type of a set, or the target of a function

variables.stands_for: a field or an ordered field
variables.note: also used for a family of sets in the set-theory files, never in the same file
any type satisfying the natural-number interface

variables.stands_for: a collection: a set of sets

variables.letters: x, y, z, a, b, c

variables.stands_for: a positive element of an ordered field

variables.note: names of proofs begin with h

deviations.why: no notation yet for the union of a collection
a type is not a set; the set of all its elements has a name
the supremum is a relation until a function is defined
the inverse is a total function; its value at 0 is unspecified, so inverse lemmas assume a nonzero element
a natural number is sent into a field by an explicit map
successor is primitive; addition is defined from it
the natural numbers here start at 0; Landau's and Feferman's start at 1

names.meaning: the least element of a set
the greatest element of a set
the least upper bound (supremum) of a set
the greatest lower bound (infimum) of a set
a set that has an upper bound
a set that has a lower bound

rules.statement: A major concept has a readable full name. Where its Lean name is abbreviated, the Lean name is the definition and the full name is an `abbrev` for it. Lemmas have one name, after the Lean name.
Every theorem, lemma, corollary, proposition and example is proved with a `by` tactic block, so that the proof can be stepped through in the InfoView.
A file that only re-exports its folder is named <Folder>Aggregator.lean and contains imports and a module docstring, no declarations.
Mathematics is declared in `namespace Aim`. A sub-namespace exists only when it is the name of a type and holds that type's own operations.

exceptions.reason: syntax macros, declared at the root
to be rewritten under Logic/Propositional; see Aim/Logic/logic-todo.md

rules.statement: A file under Aim/ imports the interface files it needs, never the root module `Aim`, which also brings in every construction.
Nothing under Aim/ or tests/ imports Mathlib. Mathlib appears only in validation/mathlib.
A variable that is a set, a collection or a family of sets is an uppercase letter. An element of a set is a lowercase letter.
Subtraction and division on a field are the derived operations. A construction of a number system never defines its own.
A proof cites the lemmas of an interface (membership lemmas for sets, the two equations for `recurse`) and does not unfold its definitions.
A `sorry` marks a proof still to be written by the learner. It is never a defect.
